entries.title: Errors that travel in families, and a more expressive site design
entries.summary: A wrong figure in a mathematics book renders perfectly and reads plausibly — so this release went looking for the ones already in the library, found that they arrive in groups, and rebuilt the four pages around what a reader is actually doing.

entries.title: The Rome and Late Antiquity shelf takes shape
entries.summary: Thirty-three Roman and late-antique texts arrive clean, history enters the library, the Grand Tour gains its second section — and the reader learns to tell you where you are.

entries.title: Deep links, language modes, and a fuller shelf
entries.summary: Link straight to a proposition, choose your language in bilingual texts, and nine new acquisitions — including the Organon.

entries.title: Mobile, performance, and a rounder Ancient Greece
entries.summary: Long texts load fast on phones and tablets, a mobile navigation menu, and recommended passages filled in across the Ancient Greece section.

entries.title: Frontend rework and the first sequenced section
entries.summary: New design language, library-catalog Explore, context-aware readers, and Ancient Greece sequenced as the first Grand Tour section.
